original_datasets.name: AEJApp-2009-0289 household data

summary_statistics.info: 1666 rows, 85 columns. Key types include category (e.g., caste), float32/float64 (e.g., village, totinc), integers.

original_datasets.notes: Household-level outcomes and attributes. The analysis uses hhcode, village, caste, and totinc. Will be merged with village.dta on village.

original_datasets.name: AEJApp-2009-0289 village data

summary_statistics.info: 122 rows, 30 columns. domhigh has 90 non-missing values. village is numeric ID.

original_datasets.notes: Provides village-level dominance indicator domhigh (1=high-caste dominated, 0=low-caste dominated). Merged to household data by village and filtered to domhigh in {0,1}.

tasks.task_instruction: Conduct the analysis without additional restriction.

analysis_path.path_description: Merge household and village data, keep villages with domhigh 0/1, and fit a mixed model: totinc ~ caste + domhigh + caste:domhigh with random intercept for village.
preprocessing_steps: Select hhcode, village, caste, totinc from household.
Drop rows missing totinc, caste, domhigh, or village.

key_choices.outcome_measure: totinc (total income at the household level).
key_choices.main_predictor_measure: domhigh (village dominance: 1=high-caste dominated, 0=low-caste dominated) and its interaction with caste.
key_choices.sample_restriction: Keep observations where domhigh is 0 or 1.
key_choices.missing_data_rule: Listwise deletion on totinc, caste, domhigh, village.
key_choices.data_processing: Merge household and village data on village; encode categorical variables via design matrix (C()).
key_choices.model_choice: Linear mixed-effects regression with random intercept for village.

main_predictor.name: domhigh
main_predictor.definition: Village-level dominance indicator (1=high-caste dominated, 0=low-caste dominated). Interacted with caste.

analysis_code.notes: Python translation of R script data/analysis_task_1.R. Writes results to /app/data/results_task1.txt.

tasks.notes_for_agent: Follow this planned path; do not change the focal claim, dataset, or analysis goal.

tasks.task_instruction: Do not include District, Crop, Distance, Groundwater, Public goods controls; do not include Irrigation, credit, and tenancy variables or their interactions; do not use instruments for water buyer status.

analysis_path.path_description: Same mixed model as Task1 and additionally compute an omnibus test for the dominance effect (approximated via OLS with village fixed effects and ANOVA on C(domhigh)).
preprocessing_steps: Select hhcode, village, caste, totinc from household.
Drop rows missing totinc, caste, domhigh, or village.

key_choices.main_predictor_measure: domhigh (village dominance: 1=high-caste dominated, 0=low-caste dominated), with interaction by caste.
key_choices.sample_restriction: Keep observations where domhigh is 0 or 1.
key_choices.missing_data_rule: Listwise deletion on totinc, caste, domhigh, village.
key_choices.data_processing: Merge household and village data on village; encode categorical variables via C(); for omnibus test, add village fixed effects via C(village) in an OLS and run ANOVA.
key_choices.model_choice: Linear mixed-effects regression with random intercept for village; OLS with village fixed effects for omnibus ANOVA.

main_predictor.name: domhigh
main_predictor.definition: Village-level dominance indicator (1=high-caste dominated, 0=low-caste dominated). Interacted with caste.

analysis_code.notes: Python translation of R script data/analysis_task_2.R. Writes mixed model summary and an ANOVA table for C(domhigh) to /app/data/results_task2.txt.

tasks.notes_for_agent: Use the planned mixed model; do not add prohibited controls or instruments. Include the omnibus dominance test as specified.

files.data/analysis_task_1__py.py: Python script executing Task1: merges datasets, filters domhigh in {0,1}, fits MixedLM totinc ~ C(caste) + C(domhigh) + C(caste):C(domhigh) with random intercept for village; outputs /app/data/results_task1.txt.
files.data/analysis_task_2__py.py: Python script executing Task2: same MixedLM as Task1 and an additional OLS with village fixed effects for ANOVA on C(domhigh); outputs /app/data/results_task2.txt.

codebase.notes: These Python scripts are translations of the provided R scripts (data/analysis_task_1.R and data/analysis_task_2.R). They assume that the entire study data directory is mounted at /app/data so that AEJApp-2009-0289-data is available at /app/data/AEJApp-2009-0289-data.

analysis.instructions: Execute Task1 and Task2 on the original AEJApp-2009-0289 household and village datasets. Use the Python translation scripts to run the mixed-effects models and produce text outputs for coefficients and omnibus tests.
allowed_actions: make bounded implementation fixes (paths, dependencies, extraction)
write compact result extraction scripts if needed
not_allowed_actions: replace the planned path with a different analysis path

debugging_rule.repair_scope: fix dependency, file path, or output extraction issues only; do not redesign the analysis

analysis.comparison_metrics: Mixed model fixed-effect coefficients and p-values for C(domhigh) and C(caste):C(domhigh); omnibus test (ANOVA) p-value for C(domhigh); conclusion text indicating whether higher income is observed for low-caste households in low- vs. high-caste dominated villages.
